description.p: Ripples keeps folders on your device in sync with Nextcloud. It is built for GNOME and Phosh, and adapts from phones to desktops.

ul.li: Sign in with Nextcloud's login flow, or use an account from GNOME Online Accounts
Several folder pairs per account, each two-way, upload only or download only
Changes noticed at once on your device, and on the server when it supports push
Renames and moves are replayed instead of uploaded again, and every transfer is atomic
Conflicts shown with both versions' details and four ways to resolve them
Exclusion patterns, excluded folders, .no-sync files and a file size limit
Optional pausing on metered connections and in power saver mode
Tray icon, start at login and syncing in the background

description.p: Folder moves and a tidier Session tab.

ul.li: A directory that disappears locally is left alone for 15 seconds, so a move is recognized as a rename and is not synced as a deletion
The Session tab's log uses the interface font, and View Full Log sits in the same group as the log
